inventoryRule: operations must equal the routes actually registered by sourceModules (tests/contract/ws27-contracts.test.ts compares against Fastify onRoute).
sharedBehaviors: Participation is decided by the ledger row (expert_member_id or customer_member_id), never by a client flag. A non-participant gets 404 LEDGER_NOT_FOUND so the ledger's existence is not disclosed.
Ordering is (created_at DESC, id DESC). The id tiebreak keeps a total order for rows written in the same millisecond.
before is the id of the last message already seen. The server resolves it inside the same ledger and returns strictly older rows, so pages have no duplicates or gaps.
Query values arrive as strings because the app runs with ajv coerceTypes:false; numeric bounds are enforced in the handler (limit > 100 => 400 INVALID_LIMIT).

Deletion (WS-25): a member may delete only their own message. A deleted message disappears from the sender's own list, while the other participant keeps the row as a tombstone { deleted: true, body: null }. The body text is never returned to the other participant and the audit entry records ids only. Re-deleting an already deleted message is 409 MESSAGE_ALREADY_DELETED (deliberately not 404, so a retry is distinguishable from a wrong id).
total counts the rows visible to the caller (own tombstones excluded), so it never disagrees with what paging can return.
All routes respond with Cache-Control: no-store and X-Server-Time.

errors.when: schema violation (missing/too long body, unknown property, bad uuid)
body is only whitespace (passes minLength, violates the table trim CHECK)
ledger does not exist or caller is not a participant

operations.notes: Default limit 50, maximum 100. nextCursor is null when the page is the last one. total uses the same visibility predicate as the page query.

errors.when: limit is not an integer in 1..100
before is unknown or belongs to another ledger
schema violation (bad uuid, limit not matching ^[1-9][0-9]{0,2}$)
ledger does not exist or caller is not a participant

operations.notes: Soft delete: sets deleted_at and returns the tombstone row (body null, deleted true). The response is sent after COMMIT so an immediate re-read cannot miss the deletion.

errors.when: the message belongs to the other participant
ledger does not exist or caller is not a participant
message does not exist in this ledger

openItems: Retention/restoration of deleted bodies is OPEN and deliberately not implemented: deleted_at is set and the text stays in the column. No purge or restore route exists.
read_at is returned but no route marks messages as read yet.
No retention/purge policy is defined for chat messages.

Message.description: Wire projection of messageColumns: deleted is derived from deleted_at, and body is null whenever the row is deleted so the text cannot leak through any read path.
